Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: this is Thursday, the ninth of the month of Muharram in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (1416 AH), and it is the second session of this year. We begin with the explanation of the words of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1].

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake, and the earth throws out its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1-4]. The words ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ are the answer to the conditional clause.

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾: what is meant by this is what Allah mentioned in His words: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [Al-Hajj 1-2].

And His words ﴿its (final) earthquake﴾ mean the great earthquake, the like of which has never been. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾, meaning that from the intensity of their bewilderment and what has befallen them, you will find them as though they were intoxicated, yet they are not intoxicated; rather they are sober, but because of the severity of the terror a person becomes as though he were drunk, not knowing how to act or what to do.

﴿And the earth throws out its burdens﴾: by "its burdens" is meant the people of the graves. When ﴿the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], they will come out of their graves to the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said: ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 6].

﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: ﴿man﴾ here refers to the species; that is, a human being says, "What is wrong with it?! What has happened to this earth, this earthquake?!" Because it comes out, and as Allah said, it is as if he were intoxicated, so he says, "What has happened to it? What is its state?!" due to the severity of the terror.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when it is shaken, ﴿it will report its news﴾, meaning it will inform of what people did upon it, of good or evil. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that "when the muezzin calls the adhan, no tree, clod, stone, or anything that hears his voice fails to bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection"[[Ibn Khuzaymah (389) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: "If you are in the desert, raise your voice with the call to prayer, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'No tree, clod, or stone hears his voice, nor jinn nor man, but it will bear witness for him.'"]]. So the earth will bear witness to what was done upon it of good or evil. This testimony is for the sake of showing the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He, glory be to Him, does not hold people to account except for what they did. Otherwise, Allah, may He be exalted, encompasses all things, and it would suffice for Him to tell His servants, Mighty and Majestic: "You did such-and-such and such-and-such." But it is by way of establishing justice and of leaving no room for the criminal to deny, for the wrongdoers deny that they were polytheists. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [Al-An'am 23]; because when they see the people of monotheism saved from punishment and delivered from it, they deny associating partners with Allah, hoping they may be saved. But their mouths will be sealed, the hands will speak, the feet will bear witness, and the skins too, and the tongues; all of them will bear witness against a person for what he did. At that time he cannot persist in his denial; rather he acknowledges and confesses, though regret will not benefit him at that time.

And His words ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 5]: that is, because Allah has inspired it; meaning He has permitted it to report its news. He, glory be to Him, is capable of all things; when He commands a thing with a command, it must come to pass. Allah addresses inanimate matter and it speaks, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat 11]. And "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to the pen: 'Write.' It said: 'My Lord, what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'"[[al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1572) narrated from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'" It was also narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (3319) from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, in similar wording.]] And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿This Day We shall seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin 65]. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, directs speech to a thing, even if it is inanimate, it addresses Allah and speaks. For this reason He said: ﴿On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it﴾.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when the earth is shaken with its earthquake, ﴿people will come forth in scattered groups﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6], that is, in separate companies, each heading to his destination. The people of Paradise, may Allah make us and you among them, head toward it, and the people of the Fire, we seek refuge with Allah, are driven toward it: ﴿On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd. They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 85-87]. So people will come forth in companies and groups, of various kinds that differ greatly, as Allah said: ﴿See how We have favoured some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction﴾ [Al-Isra' 21].

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6]: meaning they come forth in scattered groups so that their deeds are shown to them. Allah shows them their deeds, whether good, then good, or evil, then evil. This is by reckoning and by the Book: a person is given his book either in his right hand or in his left, and then he is reckoned according to what is in this book; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call him to account. "As for the believer, Allah will be alone with him and will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'You did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such,' until he acknowledges and confesses. When he sees that he is ruined, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' As for the disbeliever—we seek refuge with Allah—he is not treated in this manner; rather he is called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 18]."[[al-Bukhari (4685), and Muslim (2768/52), narrated from Safwan ibn Muhriz who said: While Ibn Umar was circumambulating the Ka'bah, a man approached and said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman—or he said: O Ibn Umar—did you hear the Prophet ﷺ speak about private conferring (najwa)?" He said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The believer will be brought near to his Lord'—Hisham said: 'the believer will draw near'—'until He places His screen (kanaf) over him and makes him acknowledge his sins: Do you know such-and-such a sin? He says: I know. He says: My Lord, I know. Twice. Then He says: I concealed it in the world, and I forgive it for you today. Then the record of his good deeds is folded up. As for the others—or the disbelievers—they are called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord...﴾ [Hud 18]."]]

And His words ﴿that they may be shown their deeds﴾: this is general (muḍāf), and a general construction implies totality. Its apparent meaning is that they will be shown both small and great deeds, and so it is, except what Allah had already forgiven, by good deeds, supplication or the like; that is erased, as He said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud 114]. Thus a person is shown his deed, both small and great, until the matter becomes clear to him, and he is given his book and told: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra' 14]. For this reason, a person must not undertake anything that does not please Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because he knows that it is recorded against him and that he will be held to account for it.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 7-8]. The word "man" (man) in the conditional construction indicates generality; that is: any person who does an atom's weight, he will see it, whether it is good or evil.

﴿Atom's weight﴾ means the weight of a dharrah (a speck). By the dharrah is meant the tiny ant, as is well known, and it does not mean the "atom" commonly understood today, as some have claimed; because this atom known today was not known at that time, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addresses people only in what they understand. He mentioned the dharrah because it is the proverbial example of smallness, as Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [An-Nisa' 40]. It is well known that whoever does even less than a dharrah will find it; but since the dharrah is the proverbial example of smallness, Allah said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.﴾

His words, may He be blessed and exalted, ﴿atom's weight﴾ indicate that what is weighed is the deeds. Scholars differ on this matter. Some scholars say that what is weighed is the deed itself; some say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds; and some say that what is weighed is the doer himself. Each has its evidence:

As for those who say that what is weighed is the deed, they cite this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, since the sense of the verse is: whoever does a deed of an atom's weight. They also cite the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7563) and Muslim (2694/31), from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] As you see, this view has evidence from the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

However, it is problematic, since a deed is not a body that can be placed in a scale; a deed is an action that has ended and passed. But this can be answered by saying: a person must believe what Allah and His Messenger have reported of the unseen matters, even if his intellect may be perplexed by it and wonder, "How can this be?" He must affirm it, because Allah's power is beyond what can be imagined. This is the first answer to this objection. Have you grasped the objection? It is: how can a deed be weighed when it is a meaning and a movement that has ended?

It is said: it is obligatory for the Muslim to submit and surrender, and not to say "How?", because the matters of the unseen are beyond what can be imagined. That is the first point.

Second: Allah makes these deeds into bodies that are placed on the scale and become heavy or light; and Allah is capable of making abstract matters into bodies, as is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning "death being brought in the form of a ram, and it is stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called; and it is said: 'O people of the Fire!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called. Then they are asked: 'Do you recognise this?' They say: 'Yes, this is death.'" —even though it appears in the form of a ram, and death is a meaning, not a body; but Allah makes it a body on the Day of Resurrection, so this death becomes that. "It is slaughtered before them, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death; and O people of the Fire, eternity with no death.'"[[al-Bukhari (4730) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram. A caller will call: 'O people of Paradise!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. Then he calls: 'O people of the Fire!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. It is slaughtered, and then he says: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death; O people of the Fire, eternity without death...'" The hadith.]] With this, the objection to this view is removed; what is the view? That what is weighed is the deed.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds, they cite the hadith of the man of the card (bitaqah): "A man will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Look at your deeds.' Great registers will be unrolled for him, containing evil deeds. When he sees that he is lost, a small card will be brought to him on which is written: 'There is no god but Allah.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' It will be said: 'You will not be wronged in anything.' Then the card is placed on one pan and the registers on the other, and the card outweighs them, and it is: 'There is no god but Allah.'"[[al-Tirmidhi (2639) narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will single out a man from my community before all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine registers will be unfolded for him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then He will say: 'Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Do you have an excuse?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Yes, you have a good deed with Us, for no wrong will be done to you today.' Then a card will come out on which is written: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' He will say: 'Bring your weighing.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' He will say: 'You will not be wronged.' He said: The registers will be placed on one pan and the card on the other, and the registers will be outweighed and the card will be heavier, for nothing is heavier than the name of Allah."]] They say: this is evidence that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the doer himself, they cite the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he was one day with the Prophet ﷺ when a strong wind blew, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud stood up, and the wind kept blowing him over, for he had thin legs and shins, so the people began to laugh. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Why do you laugh?! Or: why do you wonder?! By Him in whose hand is my soul, his two shins in the Scale are heavier than Uhud.'"[[Ahmad (3990) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was gathering a miswak from the arak tree, and he had thin legs, and the wind kept blowing him over, so the people laughed at him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Why do you laugh?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, because of the thinness of his legs." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the Scale than Uhud."]] This shows that what is weighed is the doer.

It is said: we take the first view, that what is weighed is the deed; but perhaps for some people their scrolls of deeds are weighed, and for some people they themselves are weighed.

If someone says: according to this view, that what is weighed is the deed, does this imply that people's bodies in this world matter, and that the person with a large, great body will have a heavier scale on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: No, it does not depend on bodies in this world. A man who is fat, coarse, large, and broad-bodied will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed his two shins will be heavier in the scale than Uhud." So what counts is the weight or lightness on the Day of Resurrection according to the righteous deeds one carried. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7). And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

* In this entire surah: a warning and a fear of the earth's quaking.
* In it: an encouragement to righteous deeds.
* In it: that deeds are not lost, however small, even if it is the weight of an atom or less, for a person will surely see it and it will be made known to him on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Atom's weight﴾ means the weight of a dharrah (a speck). They also cite the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7563) and Muslim (2694/31), from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] As you see, this view has evidence from the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

However, it is problematic, since a deed is not a body that can be placed in a scale; a deed is an action that has ended and passed. But this can be answered by saying: a person must believe what Allah and His Messenger have reported of the unseen matters, even if his intellect may be perplexed by it and wonder, "How can this be?" He must affirm it, because Allah's power is beyond what can be imagined. This is the first answer to this objection. Have you grasped the objection? It is: how can a deed be weighed when it is a meaning and a movement that has ended?

It is said: it is obligatory for the Muslim to submit and surrender, and not to say "How?", because the matters of the unseen are beyond what can be imagined. That is the first point.

Second: Allah makes these deeds into bodies that are placed on the scale and become heavy or light; and Allah is capable of making abstract matters into bodies, as is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning "death being brought in the form of a ram, and it is stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called; and it is said: 'O people of the Fire!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called. Then they are asked: 'Do you recognise this?' They say: 'Yes, this is death.'" —even though it appears in the form of a ram, and death is a meaning, not a body; but Allah makes it a body on the Day of Resurrection, so this death becomes that. "It is slaughtered before them, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death; and O people of the Fire, eternity with no death.'"[[al-Bukhari (4730) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram. A caller will call: 'O people of Paradise!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. Then he calls: 'O people of the Fire!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. It is slaughtered, and then he says: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death; O people of the Fire, eternity without death...'" The hadith.]] With this, the objection to this view is removed; what is the view? That what is weighed is the deed.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds, they cite the hadith of the man of the card (bitaqah): "A man will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Look at your deeds.' Great registers will be unrolled for him, containing evil deeds. When he sees that he is lost, a small card will be brought to him on which is written: 'There is no god but Allah.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' It will be said: 'You will not be wronged in anything.' Then the card is placed on one pan and the registers on the other, and the card outweighs them, and it is: 'There is no god but Allah.'"[[al-Tirmidhi (2639) narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will single out a man from my community before all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine registers will be unfolded for him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then He will say: 'Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Do you have an excuse?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Yes, you have a good deed with Us, for no wrong will be done to you today.' Then a card will come out on which is written: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' He will say: 'Bring your weighing.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' He will say: 'You will not be wronged.' He said: The registers will be placed on one pan and the card on the other, and the registers will be outweighed and the card will be heavier, for nothing is heavier than the name of Allah."]] They say: this is evidence that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the doer himself, they cite the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he was one day with the Prophet ﷺ when a strong wind blew, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud stood up, and the wind kept blowing him over, for he had thin legs and shins, so the people began to laugh. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Why do you laugh?! Or: why do you wonder?! By Him in whose hand is my soul, his two shins in the Scale are heavier than Uhud.'"[[Ahmad (3990) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was gathering a miswak from the arak tree, and he had thin legs, and the wind kept blowing him over, so the people laughed at him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Why do you laugh?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, because of the thinness of his legs." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the Scale than Uhud."]] This shows that what is weighed is the doer.

It is said: we take the first view, that what is weighed is the deed; but perhaps for some people their scrolls of deeds are weighed, and for some people they themselves are weighed.

If someone says: according to this view, that what is weighed is the deed, does this imply that people's bodies in this world matter, and that the person with a large, great body will have a heavier scale on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: No, it does not depend on bodies in this world. A man who is fat, coarse, large, and broad-bodied will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed his two shins will be heavier in the scale than Uhud." So what counts is the weight or lightness on the Day of Resurrection according to the righteous deeds one carried. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7). And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

* In this entire surah: a warning and a fear of the earth's quaking.
* In it: an encouragement to righteous deeds.
* In it: that deeds are not lost, however small, even if it is the weight of an atom or less, for a person will surely see it and it will be made known to him on the Day of Resurrection.

We ask Allah, exalted is He, to conclude for us and for you with goodness, happiness, righteousness, and success, and to make us among those who are gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation, indeed He is over all things capable.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: this is Thursday, the ninth of the month of Muharram in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (1416 AH), and it is the second session of this year. We begin with the explanation of the words of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1].

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake, and the earth throws out its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1-4]. The words ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ are the answer to the conditional clause.

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾: what is meant by this is what Allah mentioned in His words: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [Al-Hajj 1-2].

And His words ﴿its (final) earthquake﴾ mean the great earthquake, the like of which has never been. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾, meaning that from the intensity of their bewilderment and what has befallen them, you will find them as though they were intoxicated, yet they are not intoxicated; rather they are sober, but because of the severity of the terror a person becomes as though he were drunk, not knowing how to act or what to do.

﴿And the earth throws out its burdens﴾: by "its burdens" is meant the people of the graves. When ﴿the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], they will come out of their graves to the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said: ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 6].

﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: ﴿man﴾ here refers to the species; that is, a human being says, "What is wrong with it?! What has happened to this earth, this earthquake?!" Because it comes out, and as Allah said, it is as if he were intoxicated, so he says, "What has happened to it? What is its state?!" due to the severity of the terror.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when it is shaken, ﴿it will report its news﴾, meaning it will inform of what people did upon it, of good or evil. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that "when the muezzin calls the adhan, no tree, clod, stone, or anything that hears his voice fails to bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection"[[Ibn Khuzaymah (389) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: "If you are in the desert, raise your voice with the call to prayer, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'No tree, clod, or stone hears his voice, nor jinn nor man, but it will bear witness for him.'"]]. So the earth will bear witness to what was done upon it of good or evil. This testimony is for the sake of showing the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He, glory be to Him, does not hold people to account except for what they did. Otherwise, Allah, may He be exalted, encompasses all things, and it would suffice for Him to tell His servants, Mighty and Majestic: "You did such-and-such and such-and-such." But it is by way of establishing justice and of leaving no room for the criminal to deny, for the wrongdoers deny that they were polytheists. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [Al-An'am 23]; because when they see the people of monotheism saved from punishment and delivered from it, they deny associating partners with Allah, hoping they may be saved. But their mouths will be sealed, the hands will speak, the feet will bear witness, and the skins too, and the tongues; all of them will bear witness against a person for what he did. At that time he cannot persist in his denial; rather he acknowledges and confesses, though regret will not benefit him at that time.

And His words ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 5]: that is, because Allah has inspired it; meaning He has permitted it to report its news. He, glory be to Him, is capable of all things; when He commands a thing with a command, it must come to pass. Allah addresses inanimate matter and it speaks, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat 11]. And "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to the pen: 'Write.' It said: 'My Lord, what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'"[[al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1572) narrated from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'" It was also narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (3319) from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, in similar wording.]] And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿This Day We shall seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin 65]. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, directs speech to a thing, even if it is inanimate, it addresses Allah and speaks. For this reason He said: ﴿On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it﴾.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when the earth is shaken with its earthquake, ﴿people will come forth in scattered groups﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6], that is, in separate companies, each heading to his destination. The people of Paradise, may Allah make us and you among them, head toward it, and the people of the Fire, we seek refuge with Allah, are driven toward it: ﴿On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd. They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 85-87]. So people will come forth in companies and groups, of various kinds that differ greatly, as Allah said: ﴿See how We have favoured some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction﴾ [Al-Isra' 21].

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6]: meaning they come forth in scattered groups so that their deeds are shown to them. Allah shows them their deeds, whether good, then good, or evil, then evil. This is by reckoning and by the Book: a person is given his book either in his right hand or in his left, and then he is reckoned according to what is in this book; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call him to account. "As for the believer, Allah will be alone with him and will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'You did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such,' until he acknowledges and confesses. When he sees that he is ruined, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' As for the disbeliever—we seek refuge with Allah—he is not treated in this manner; rather he is called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 18]."[[al-Bukhari (4685), and Muslim (2768/52), narrated from Safwan ibn Muhriz who said: While Ibn Umar was circumambulating the Ka'bah, a man approached and said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman—or he said: O Ibn Umar—did you hear the Prophet ﷺ speak about private conferring (najwa)?" He said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The believer will be brought near to his Lord'—Hisham said: 'the believer will draw near'—'until He places His screen (kanaf) over him and makes him acknowledge his sins: Do you know such-and-such a sin? He says: I know. He says: My Lord, I know. Twice. Then He says: I concealed it in the world, and I forgive it for you today. Then the record of his good deeds is folded up. As for the others—or the disbelievers—they are called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord...﴾ [Hud 18]."]]

And His words ﴿that they may be shown their deeds﴾: this is general (muḍāf), and a general construction implies totality. Its apparent meaning is that they will be shown both small and great deeds, and so it is, except what Allah had already forgiven, by good deeds, supplication or the like; that is erased, as He said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud 114]. Thus a person is shown his deed, both small and great, until the matter becomes clear to him, and he is given his book and told: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra' 14]. For this reason, a person must not undertake anything that does not please Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because he knows that it is recorded against him and that he will be held to account for it.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 7-8]. The word "man" (man) in the conditional construction indicates generality; that is: any person who does an atom's weight, he will see it, whether it is good or evil.

﴿Atom's weight﴾ means the weight of a dharrah (a speck). By the dharrah is meant the tiny ant, as is well known, and it does not mean the "atom" commonly understood today, as some have claimed; because this atom known today was not known at that time, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addresses people only in what they understand. He mentioned the dharrah because it is the proverbial example of smallness, as Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [An-Nisa' 40]. It is well known that whoever does even less than a dharrah will find it; but since the dharrah is the proverbial example of smallness, Allah said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.﴾

His words, may He be blessed and exalted, ﴿atom's weight﴾ indicate that what is weighed is the deeds. Scholars differ on this matter. Some scholars say that what is weighed is the deed itself; some say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds; and some say that what is weighed is the doer himself. Each has its evidence:

As for those who say that what is weighed is the deed, they cite this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, since the sense of the verse is: whoever does a deed of an atom's weight. They also cite the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7563) and Muslim (2694/31), from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] As you see, this view has evidence from the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

However, it is problematic, since a deed is not a body that can be placed in a scale; a deed is an action that has ended and passed. But this can be answered by saying: a person must believe what Allah and His Messenger have reported of the unseen matters, even if his intellect may be perplexed by it and wonder, "How can this be?" He must affirm it, because Allah's power is beyond what can be imagined. This is the first answer to this objection. Have you grasped the objection? It is: how can a deed be weighed when it is a meaning and a movement that has ended?

It is said: it is obligatory for the Muslim to submit and surrender, and not to say "How?", because the matters of the unseen are beyond what can be imagined. That is the first point.

Second: Allah makes these deeds into bodies that are placed on the scale and become heavy or light; and Allah is capable of making abstract matters into bodies, as is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning "death being brought in the form of a ram, and it is stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called; and it is said: 'O people of the Fire!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called. Then they are asked: 'Do you recognise this?' They say: 'Yes, this is death.'" —even though it appears in the form of a ram, and death is a meaning, not a body; but Allah makes it a body on the Day of Resurrection, so this death becomes that. "It is slaughtered before them, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death; and O people of the Fire, eternity with no death.'"[[al-Bukhari (4730) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram. A caller will call: 'O people of Paradise!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. Then he calls: 'O people of the Fire!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. It is slaughtered, and then he says: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death; O people of the Fire, eternity without death...'" The hadith.]] With this, the objection to this view is removed; what is the view? That what is weighed is the deed.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds, they cite the hadith of the man of the card (bitaqah): "A man will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Look at your deeds.' Great registers will be unrolled for him, containing evil deeds. When he sees that he is lost, a small card will be brought to him on which is written: 'There is no god but Allah.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' It will be said: 'You will not be wronged in anything.' Then the card is placed on one pan and the registers on the other, and the card outweighs them, and it is: 'There is no god but Allah.'"[[al-Tirmidhi (2639) narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will single out a man from my community before all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine registers will be unfolded for him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then He will say: 'Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Do you have an excuse?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Yes, you have a good deed with Us, for no wrong will be done to you today.' Then a card will come out on which is written: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' He will say: 'Bring your weighing.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' He will say: 'You will not be wronged.' He said: The registers will be placed on one pan and the card on the other, and the registers will be outweighed and the card will be heavier, for nothing is heavier than the name of Allah."]] They say: this is evidence that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the doer himself, they cite the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he was one day with the Prophet ﷺ when a strong wind blew, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud stood up, and the wind kept blowing him over, for he had thin legs and shins, so the people began to laugh. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Why do you laugh?! Or: why do you wonder?! By Him in whose hand is my soul, his two shins in the Scale are heavier than Uhud.'"[[Ahmad (3990) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was gathering a miswak from the arak tree, and he had thin legs, and the wind kept blowing him over, so the people laughed at him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Why do you laugh?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, because of the thinness of his legs." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the Scale than Uhud."]] This shows that what is weighed is the doer.

It is said: we take the first view, that what is weighed is the deed; but perhaps for some people their scrolls of deeds are weighed, and for some people they themselves are weighed.

If someone says: according to this view, that what is weighed is the deed, does this imply that people's bodies in this world matter, and that the person with a large, great body will have a heavier scale on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: No, it does not depend on bodies in this world. A man who is fat, coarse, large, and broad-bodied will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed his two shins will be heavier in the scale than Uhud." So what counts is the weight or lightness on the Day of Resurrection according to the righteous deeds one carried. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7). And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

* In this entire surah: a warning and a fear of the earth's quaking.
* In it: an encouragement to righteous deeds.
* In it: that deeds are not lost, however small, even if it is the weight of an atom or less, for a person will surely see it and it will be made known to him on the Day of Resurrection.

We ask Allah, exalted is He, to conclude for us and for you with goodness, happiness, righteousness, and success, and to make us among those who are gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation, indeed He is over all things capable.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: this is Thursday, the ninth of the month of Muharram in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (1416 AH), and it is the second session of this year. We begin with the explanation of the words of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1].

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake, and the earth throws out its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1-4]. The words ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ are the answer to the conditional clause.

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾: what is meant by this is what Allah mentioned in His words: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [Al-Hajj 1-2].

And His words ﴿its (final) earthquake﴾ mean the great earthquake, the like of which has never been. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾, meaning that from the intensity of their bewilderment and what has befallen them, you will find them as though they were intoxicated, yet they are not intoxicated; rather they are sober, but because of the severity of the terror a person becomes as though he were drunk, not knowing how to act or what to do.

﴿And the earth throws out its burdens﴾: by "its burdens" is meant the people of the graves. When ﴿the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], they will come out of their graves to the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said: ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 6].

﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: ﴿man﴾ here refers to the species; that is, a human being says, "What is wrong with it?! What has happened to this earth, this earthquake?!" Because it comes out, and as Allah said, it is as if he were intoxicated, so he says, "What has happened to it? What is its state?!" due to the severity of the terror.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when it is shaken, ﴿it will report its news﴾, meaning it will inform of what people did upon it, of good or evil. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that "when the muezzin calls the adhan, no tree, clod, stone, or anything that hears his voice fails to bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection"[[Ibn Khuzaymah (389) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: "If you are in the desert, raise your voice with the call to prayer, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'No tree, clod, or stone hears his voice, nor jinn nor man, but it will bear witness for him.'"]]. So the earth will bear witness to what was done upon it of good or evil. This testimony is for the sake of showing the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He, glory be to Him, does not hold people to account except for what they did. Otherwise, Allah, may He be exalted, encompasses all things, and it would suffice for Him to tell His servants, Mighty and Majestic: "You did such-and-such and such-and-such." But it is by way of establishing justice and of leaving no room for the criminal to deny, for the wrongdoers deny that they were polytheists. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [Al-An'am 23]; because when they see the people of monotheism saved from punishment and delivered from it, they deny associating partners with Allah, hoping they may be saved. But their mouths will be sealed, the hands will speak, the feet will bear witness, and the skins too, and the tongues; all of them will bear witness against a person for what he did. At that time he cannot persist in his denial; rather he acknowledges and confesses, though regret will not benefit him at that time.

And His words ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 5]: that is, because Allah has inspired it; meaning He has permitted it to report its news. He, glory be to Him, is capable of all things; when He commands a thing with a command, it must come to pass. Allah addresses inanimate matter and it speaks, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat 11]. And "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to the pen: 'Write.' It said: 'My Lord, what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'"[[al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1572) narrated from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'" It was also narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (3319) from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, in similar wording.]] And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿This Day We shall seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin 65]. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, directs speech to a thing, even if it is inanimate, it addresses Allah and speaks. For this reason He said: ﴿On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it﴾.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when the earth is shaken with its earthquake, ﴿people will come forth in scattered groups﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6], that is, in separate companies, each heading to his destination. The people of Paradise, may Allah make us and you among them, head toward it, and the people of the Fire, we seek refuge with Allah, are driven toward it: ﴿On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd. They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 85-87]. So people will come forth in companies and groups, of various kinds that differ greatly, as Allah said: ﴿See how We have favoured some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction﴾ [Al-Isra' 21].

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6]: meaning they come forth in scattered groups so that their deeds are shown to them. Allah shows them their deeds, whether good, then good, or evil, then evil. This is by reckoning and by the Book: a person is given his book either in his right hand or in his left, and then he is reckoned according to what is in this book; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call him to account. "As for the believer, Allah will be alone with him and will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'You did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such,' until he acknowledges and confesses. When he sees that he is ruined, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' As for the disbeliever—we seek refuge with Allah—he is not treated in this manner; rather he is called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 18]."[[al-Bukhari (4685), and Muslim (2768/52), narrated from Safwan ibn Muhriz who said: While Ibn Umar was circumambulating the Ka'bah, a man approached and said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman—or he said: O Ibn Umar—did you hear the Prophet ﷺ speak about private conferring (najwa)?" He said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The believer will be brought near to his Lord'—Hisham said: 'the believer will draw near'—'until He places His screen (kanaf) over him and makes him acknowledge his sins: Do you know such-and-such a sin? He says: I know. He says: My Lord, I know. Twice. Then He says: I concealed it in the world, and I forgive it for you today. Then the record of his good deeds is folded up. As for the others—or the disbelievers—they are called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord...﴾ [Hud 18]."]]

And His words ﴿that they may be shown their deeds﴾: this is general (muḍāf), and a general construction implies totality. Its apparent meaning is that they will be shown both small and great deeds, and so it is, except what Allah had already forgiven, by good deeds, supplication or the like; that is erased, as He said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud 114]. Thus a person is shown his deed, both small and great, until the matter becomes clear to him, and he is given his book and told: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra' 14]. For this reason, a person must not undertake anything that does not please Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because he knows that it is recorded against him and that he will be held to account for it.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 7-8]. The word "man" (man) in the conditional construction indicates generality; that is: any person who does an atom's weight, he will see it, whether it is good or evil.

﴿Atom's weight﴾ means the weight of a dharrah (a speck). By the dharrah is meant the tiny ant, as is well known, and it does not mean the "atom" commonly understood today, as some have claimed; because this atom known today was not known at that time, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addresses people only in what they understand. He mentioned the dharrah because it is the proverbial example of smallness, as Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [An-Nisa' 40]. It is well known that whoever does even less than a dharrah will find it; but since the dharrah is the proverbial example of smallness, Allah said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.﴾

His words, may He be blessed and exalted, ﴿atom's weight﴾ indicate that what is weighed is the deeds. Scholars differ on this matter. Some scholars say that what is weighed is the deed itself; some say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds; and some say that what is weighed is the doer himself. Each has its evidence:

As for those who say that what is weighed is the deed, they cite this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, since the sense of the verse is: whoever does a deed of an atom's weight. They also cite the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7563) and Muslim (2694/31), from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] As you see, this view has evidence from the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

However, it is problematic, since a deed is not a body that can be placed in a scale; a deed is an action that has ended and passed. But this can be answered by saying: a person must believe what Allah and His Messenger have reported of the unseen matters, even if his intellect may be perplexed by it and wonder, "How can this be?" He must affirm it, because Allah's power is beyond what can be imagined. This is the first answer to this objection. Have you grasped the objection? It is: how can a deed be weighed when it is a meaning and a movement that has ended?

It is said: it is obligatory for the Muslim to submit and surrender, and not to say "How?", because the matters of the unseen are beyond what can be imagined. That is the first point.

Second: Allah makes these deeds into bodies that are placed on the scale and become heavy or light; and Allah is capable of making abstract matters into bodies, as is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning "death being brought in the form of a ram, and it is stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called; and it is said: 'O people of the Fire!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called. Then they are asked: 'Do you recognise this?' They say: 'Yes, this is death.'" —even though it appears in the form of a ram, and death is a meaning, not a body; but Allah makes it a body on the Day of Resurrection, so this death becomes that. "It is slaughtered before them, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death; and O people of the Fire, eternity with no death.'"[[al-Bukhari (4730) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram. A caller will call: 'O people of Paradise!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. Then he calls: 'O people of the Fire!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. It is slaughtered, and then he says: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death; O people of the Fire, eternity without death...'" The hadith.]] With this, the objection to this view is removed; what is the view? That what is weighed is the deed.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds, they cite the hadith of the man of the card (bitaqah): "A man will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Look at your deeds.' Great registers will be unrolled for him, containing evil deeds. When he sees that he is lost, a small card will be brought to him on which is written: 'There is no god but Allah.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' It will be said: 'You will not be wronged in anything.' Then the card is placed on one pan and the registers on the other, and the card outweighs them, and it is: 'There is no god but Allah.'"[[al-Tirmidhi (2639) narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will single out a man from my community before all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine registers will be unfolded for him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then He will say: 'Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Do you have an excuse?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Yes, you have a good deed with Us, for no wrong will be done to you today.' Then a card will come out on which is written: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' He will say: 'Bring your weighing.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' He will say: 'You will not be wronged.' He said: The registers will be placed on one pan and the card on the other, and the registers will be outweighed and the card will be heavier, for nothing is heavier than the name of Allah."]] They say: this is evidence that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the doer himself, they cite the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he was one day with the Prophet ﷺ when a strong wind blew, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud stood up, and the wind kept blowing him over, for he had thin legs and shins, so the people began to laugh. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Why do you laugh?! Or: why do you wonder?! By Him in whose hand is my soul, his two shins in the Scale are heavier than Uhud.'"[[Ahmad (3990) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was gathering a miswak from the arak tree, and he had thin legs, and the wind kept blowing him over, so the people laughed at him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Why do you laugh?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, because of the thinness of his legs." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the Scale than Uhud."]] This shows that what is weighed is the doer.

It is said: we take the first view, that what is weighed is the deed; but perhaps for some people their scrolls of deeds are weighed, and for some people they themselves are weighed.

If someone says: according to this view, that what is weighed is the deed, does this imply that people's bodies in this world matter, and that the person with a large, great body will have a heavier scale on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: No, it does not depend on bodies in this world. A man who is fat, coarse, large, and broad-bodied will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed his two shins will be heavier in the scale than Uhud." So what counts is the weight or lightness on the Day of Resurrection according to the righteous deeds one carried. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7). And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

* In this entire surah: a warning and a fear of the earth's quaking.
* In it: an encouragement to righteous deeds.
* In it: that deeds are not lost, however small, even if it is the weight of an atom or less, for a person will surely see it and it will be made known to him on the Day of Resurrection.

We ask Allah, exalted is He, to conclude for us and for you with goodness, happiness, righteousness, and success, and to make us among those who are gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation, indeed He is over all things capable.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: this is Thursday, the ninth of the month of Muharram in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (1416 AH), and it is the second session of this year. We begin with the explanation of the words of Allah, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1].

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake, and the earth throws out its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 1-4]. The words ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ are the answer to the conditional clause.

﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) earthquake﴾: what is meant by this is what Allah mentioned in His words: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [Al-Hajj 1-2].

And His words ﴿its (final) earthquake﴾ mean the great earthquake, the like of which has never been. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾, meaning that from the intensity of their bewilderment and what has befallen them, you will find them as though they were intoxicated, yet they are not intoxicated; rather they are sober, but because of the severity of the terror a person becomes as though he were drunk, not knowing how to act or what to do.

﴿And the earth throws out its burdens﴾: by "its burdens" is meant the people of the graves. When ﴿the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth falls unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and at once they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], they will come out of their graves to the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, said: ﴿On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 6].

﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾: ﴿man﴾ here refers to the species; that is, a human being says, "What is wrong with it?! What has happened to this earth, this earthquake?!" Because it comes out, and as Allah said, it is as if he were intoxicated, so he says, "What has happened to it? What is its state?!" due to the severity of the terror.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when it is shaken, ﴿it will report its news﴾, meaning it will inform of what people did upon it, of good or evil. It has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that "when the muezzin calls the adhan, no tree, clod, stone, or anything that hears his voice fails to bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection"[[Ibn Khuzaymah (389) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: "If you are in the desert, raise your voice with the call to prayer, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'No tree, clod, or stone hears his voice, nor jinn nor man, but it will bear witness for him.'"]]. So the earth will bear witness to what was done upon it of good or evil. This testimony is for the sake of showing the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He, glory be to Him, does not hold people to account except for what they did. Otherwise, Allah, may He be exalted, encompasses all things, and it would suffice for Him to tell His servants, Mighty and Majestic: "You did such-and-such and such-and-such." But it is by way of establishing justice and of leaving no room for the criminal to deny, for the wrongdoers deny that they were polytheists. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [Al-An'am 23]; because when they see the people of monotheism saved from punishment and delivered from it, they deny associating partners with Allah, hoping they may be saved. But their mouths will be sealed, the hands will speak, the feet will bear witness, and the skins too, and the tongues; all of them will bear witness against a person for what he did. At that time he cannot persist in his denial; rather he acknowledges and confesses, though regret will not benefit him at that time.

And His words ﴿because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 5]: that is, because Allah has inspired it; meaning He has permitted it to report its news. He, glory be to Him, is capable of all things; when He commands a thing with a command, it must come to pass. Allah addresses inanimate matter and it speaks, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth, "Come, willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat 11]. And "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to the pen: 'Write.' It said: 'My Lord, what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'"[[al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin (1572) narrated from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection.'" It was also narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (3319) from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, in similar wording.]] And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿This Day We shall seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin 65]. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, directs speech to a thing, even if it is inanimate, it addresses Allah and speaks. For this reason He said: ﴿On that Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it﴾.

﴿On that Day﴾, meaning: on the day when the earth is shaken with its earthquake, ﴿people will come forth in scattered groups﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6], that is, in separate companies, each heading to his destination. The people of Paradise, may Allah make us and you among them, head toward it, and the people of the Fire, we seek refuge with Allah, are driven toward it: ﴿On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and drive the criminals to Hell as a thirsty herd. They will not possess intercession, except one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam 85-87]. So people will come forth in companies and groups, of various kinds that differ greatly, as Allah said: ﴿See how We have favoured some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in distinction﴾ [Al-Isra' 21].

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 6]: meaning they come forth in scattered groups so that their deeds are shown to them. Allah shows them their deeds, whether good, then good, or evil, then evil. This is by reckoning and by the Book: a person is given his book either in his right hand or in his left, and then he is reckoned according to what is in this book; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will call him to account. "As for the believer, Allah will be alone with him and will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'You did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such,' until he acknowledges and confesses. When he sees that he is ruined, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' As for the disbeliever—we seek refuge with Allah—he is not treated in this manner; rather he is called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 18]."[[al-Bukhari (4685), and Muslim (2768/52), narrated from Safwan ibn Muhriz who said: While Ibn Umar was circumambulating the Ka'bah, a man approached and said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman—or he said: O Ibn Umar—did you hear the Prophet ﷺ speak about private conferring (najwa)?" He said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'The believer will be brought near to his Lord'—Hisham said: 'the believer will draw near'—'until He places His screen (kanaf) over him and makes him acknowledge his sins: Do you know such-and-such a sin? He says: I know. He says: My Lord, I know. Twice. Then He says: I concealed it in the world, and I forgive it for you today. Then the record of his good deeds is folded up. As for the others—or the disbelievers—they are called out before all the creatures: ﴿These are they who lied against their Lord...﴾ [Hud 18]."]]

And His words ﴿that they may be shown their deeds﴾: this is general (muḍāf), and a general construction implies totality. Its apparent meaning is that they will be shown both small and great deeds, and so it is, except what Allah had already forgiven, by good deeds, supplication or the like; that is erased, as He said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud 114]. Thus a person is shown his deed, both small and great, until the matter becomes clear to him, and he is given his book and told: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra' 14]. For this reason, a person must not undertake anything that does not please Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because he knows that it is recorded against him and that he will be held to account for it.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 7-8]. The word "man" (man) in the conditional construction indicates generality; that is: any person who does an atom's weight, he will see it, whether it is good or evil.

﴿Atom's weight﴾ means the weight of a dharrah (a speck). By the dharrah is meant the tiny ant, as is well known, and it does not mean the "atom" commonly understood today, as some have claimed; because this atom known today was not known at that time, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addresses people only in what they understand. He mentioned the dharrah because it is the proverbial example of smallness, as Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [An-Nisa' 40]. It is well known that whoever does even less than a dharrah will find it; but since the dharrah is the proverbial example of smallness, Allah said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.﴾

His words, may He be blessed and exalted, ﴿atom's weight﴾ indicate that what is weighed is the deeds. Scholars differ on this matter. Some scholars say that what is weighed is the deed itself; some say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds; and some say that what is weighed is the doer himself. Each has its evidence:

As for those who say that what is weighed is the deed, they cite this verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight﴾, since the sense of the verse is: whoever does a deed of an atom's weight. They also cite the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7563) and Muslim (2694/31), from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] As you see, this view has evidence from the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

However, it is problematic, since a deed is not a body that can be placed in a scale; a deed is an action that has ended and passed. But this can be answered by saying: a person must believe what Allah and His Messenger have reported of the unseen matters, even if his intellect may be perplexed by it and wonder, "How can this be?" He must affirm it, because Allah's power is beyond what can be imagined. This is the first answer to this objection. Have you grasped the objection? It is: how can a deed be weighed when it is a meaning and a movement that has ended?

It is said: it is obligatory for the Muslim to submit and surrender, and not to say "How?", because the matters of the unseen are beyond what can be imagined. That is the first point.

Second: Allah makes these deeds into bodies that are placed on the scale and become heavy or light; and Allah is capable of making abstract matters into bodies, as is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ concerning "death being brought in the form of a ram, and it is stopped between Paradise and the Fire, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called; and it is said: 'O people of the Fire!' They raise their heads and look, wondering why they were called. Then they are asked: 'Do you recognise this?' They say: 'Yes, this is death.'" —even though it appears in the form of a ram, and death is a meaning, not a body; but Allah makes it a body on the Day of Resurrection, so this death becomes that. "It is slaughtered before them, and it is said: 'O people of Paradise, eternity with no death; and O people of the Fire, eternity with no death.'"[[al-Bukhari (4730) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Death will be brought in the form of a white-speckled ram. A caller will call: 'O people of Paradise!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. Then he calls: 'O people of the Fire!' They will raise their heads and look, and he will say: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death,' and all of them have seen it. It is slaughtered, and then he says: 'O people of Paradise, eternity without death; O people of the Fire, eternity without death...'" The hadith.]] With this, the objection to this view is removed; what is the view? That what is weighed is the deed.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds, they cite the hadith of the man of the card (bitaqah): "A man will be brought forth on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Look at your deeds.' Great registers will be unrolled for him, containing evil deeds. When he sees that he is lost, a small card will be brought to him on which is written: 'There is no god but Allah.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' It will be said: 'You will not be wronged in anything.' Then the card is placed on one pan and the registers on the other, and the card outweighs them, and it is: 'There is no god but Allah.'"[[al-Tirmidhi (2639) narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will single out a man from my community before all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and ninety-nine registers will be unfolded for him, each register as far as the eye can see. Then He will say: 'Do you deny any of this? Have my recording angels wronged you?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Do you have an excuse?' He will say: 'No, my Lord.' He will say: 'Yes, you have a good deed with Us, for no wrong will be done to you today.' Then a card will come out on which is written: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' He will say: 'Bring your weighing.' He will say: 'O my Lord, what is this card with these registers?' He will say: 'You will not be wronged.' He said: The registers will be placed on one pan and the card on the other, and the registers will be outweighed and the card will be heavier, for nothing is heavier than the name of Allah."]] They say: this is evidence that what is weighed is the scrolls of deeds.

As for those who say that what is weighed is the doer himself, they cite the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he was one day with the Prophet ﷺ when a strong wind blew, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud stood up, and the wind kept blowing him over, for he had thin legs and shins, so the people began to laugh. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Why do you laugh?! Or: why do you wonder?! By Him in whose hand is my soul, his two shins in the Scale are heavier than Uhud.'"[[Ahmad (3990) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was gathering a miswak from the arak tree, and he had thin legs, and the wind kept blowing him over, so the people laughed at him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Why do you laugh?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, because of the thinness of his legs." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they are heavier in the Scale than Uhud."]] This shows that what is weighed is the doer.

It is said: we take the first view, that what is weighed is the deed; but perhaps for some people their scrolls of deeds are weighed, and for some people they themselves are weighed.

If someone says: according to this view, that what is weighed is the deed, does this imply that people's bodies in this world matter, and that the person with a large, great body will have a heavier scale on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: No, it does not depend on bodies in this world. A man who is fat, coarse, large, and broad-bodied will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed his two shins will be heavier in the scale than Uhud." So what counts is the weight or lightness on the Day of Resurrection according to the righteous deeds one carried. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7). And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

* In this entire surah: a warning and a fear of the earth's quaking.
* In it: an encouragement to righteous deeds.
* In it: that deeds are not lost, however small, even if it is the weight of an atom or less, for a person will surely see it and it will be made known to him on the Day of Resurrection.

We ask Allah, exalted is He, to conclude for us and for you with goodness, happiness, righteousness, and success, and to make us among those who are gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation, indeed He is over all things capable.
